title: Rydzewska Żaneta
name: Rydzewska Żaneta
description: composer and clarinetist; b. October 5, 1991, Ełk. She completed her studies at the Fryderyk Chopin University of Music in the composition classes of Aleksander Kościów and Stanisław Moryto, and the clarinet class of Wojciech Mrozek, as well as at the Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln in the composition class of Brigitta Muntendorf. In 2021, she furthered her education with postgraduate studies in philosophy at the University of Warsaw, and in 2026, she was awarded the degree of Doctor of Arts. She has consulted on her works during composition masterclasses with such figures as George Friedrich Haas, Wolfgang Rihm, Dieter Ammann, Francesco Filidei, Simon Steen-Andersen, Enno Poppe, Alexander Schubert, Michael Beil, Marko Nikodijevic, Caspar Johannes Walter, Carola Bauckholt, Matthew Shlomowitz, Manos Tsangaris, and Mathias Spahlinger. In 2025, she participated in Max/MSP courses at IRCAM as part of the "Young Researchers of FCUM" project. Her artistic achievements have been recognized through numerous awards and fellowships, including the Bernd-Alois-Zimmermann-Stipendium in Cologne (2019), scholarships from the Minister of Culture and National Heritage for outstanding academic and artistic results (2018/2019), the "Young Poland" scholarship (2020), as well as grants from the Marshal of the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship and the Rector of the FCUM. Her competition record includes a distinction for a work set to an Esperanto text at the "Esperanto" Music Competition (2008), second prize at the Festival of Young Creators in Białystok (2009), and distinctions at the 2nd "Patri Patrie" International Composition Competition in Katowice (2014) and the 3rd M. Stachowski National Competition for Young Composers in Kraków (2016). She received second prizes at the "...when I think Berio..." National Composition Competition in Wrocław (2015) and the FCUM Inter-University Composition Competition (2015). Furthermore, she was a laureate of the AKOM Ensemble International Call for Scores in Rotterdam and the 7th Z. Mycielski Composition Competition (2016). Her later accolades include third prize at the Stanisław Moniuszko Composition Competition in Gdańsk (2018), an Individual Prize at the IEMA Ensemble International Call for Scores (2018), and the International BTHVN Competition in Bonn (2020). In 2020, she was a laureate of "The Science of Fiction" competition organized by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute and Klangforum Wien (ex aequo with Mikołaj Laskowski). She also received the "Best Original Score" award at the WIFFEN 2022 international film festival in Nigeria for the film Last Days of Summer, directed by Klaudia Kęska, and won the Internationaler Acht Brücken Kompositionswettbewerb (2025), which led to a commission for her work Superheroines by the Kölner Philharmonie. In her compositions, she frequently references nature, physics, and philosophy, while addressing contemporary social issues and interpersonal relations. Her output focuses on instrumental music integrated with electronics, choreography, video, lighting, installations, and olfaction. Her professional experience includes collaborations with numerous renowned ensembles, such as Ensemble intercontemporain, Ensemble Modern, WDR Sinfonieorchester, Klangforum Wien, Ensemble Musikfabrik, Trio Catch, Mivos Quartet, Sinfonia Varsovia, Polish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Lüneburger Symphoniker, AUKSO, Silesian Quartet, Kwartludium, Ensemble Garage, hand werk, Schwerpunkt Ensemble, Internationale Ensemble Modern Akademie, Spółdzielnia Muzyczna, Ensemble for New Music Tallinn, United Instruments of Lucilin, electronic ID, Broken Frames Syndicate, Kollektiv3:6Koeln, AKOM Ensemble, Chopin University Modern Ensemble, and Sinfonietta Pomerania. Her works have been performed at major festivals, including Warsaw Autumn, ManiFeste (IRCAM), Wittener Tage für neue Kammermusik (WDR3), Lucerne Festival, Ultraschall Berlin, Acht Brücken, Orgel-Mixturen (Deutschlandfunk), Tampere Biennale, Sacrum Profanum, Festival of Premieres, Ad libitum, Korvat auki Helsinki, ON-Cologne, Avant Art Festival, AudioArt, T. Stańko Jazz Autumn, High Noon Musik 2000+ in Konstanz, Cluster in Lucca, Warsaw Music Meetings, and New Waves in Gdańsk. She has also participated in the ManiFeste Academy, Luxembourg Composition Academy, Lucerne Festival Academy, and Donaueschinger Musiktage "Next Generation". The composer currently teaches instrumentation and computer music composition at the Department of Composition and Music Theory of the FCUM. She served as the chair of the Youth Circle of the Polish Composers' Union (ZKP) from 2016 to 2018 and has been a member of the ZKP since 2023. As of 2026, she serves as the faculty advisor for the Youth Circle of the ZKP. In 2022, she was honored with the ZAiKS Authors' Association Award for the best composer of the young generation during the Fryderyk Awards Gala.
